_comment: Viam 103 bimanual QC cell. Two ur5e arms inspect an 80 mm carton: arm-a picks it off
the infeed belt and presents five faces to inspect-cam, hands it to arm-b, and arm-b
places it in the good or bad tray.
Geometry is the isaac-arcade layout scaled by 0.76, from probes/scale_study.py. Two
constraints have to hold at once: every station stays inside the arm's reach with
~10% margin, and both trays stay OUTSIDE arm-a's reach, which is what makes the
handoff a fact of the layout rather than an intention. The viable window is only
0.70-0.76, so rescaling without re-running the sweep will break one of them.
The reach bound in that sweep is 1016.7 mm, measured from the motion service, NOT the
850 mm on the UR5e datasheet - that figure is to the wrist centre. An earlier pass
used 850, concluded the trays were out of reach at scale 0.62, and was wrong: the
planner reached the good tray from arm-a 5/5.
Each arm's isaac 'position' and its viam 'frame.translation' describe the same point
in two units (m and mm), and the test keeps them consistent so the file reads
honestly. Note they cannot actually disagree at runtime: apply_frame_to_attrs()
overwrites 'position' from the frame, so the frame wins and 'position' is inert
whenever a frame is present. The placement risk that IS real is rotational - whether
the SVA's base frame and the Isaac USD's root share a yaw - and no config test can
see it. Phase 1 settles it by commanding all-zero joints and comparing Isaac's
end-effector world pose against motion.GetPose.
inspect-cam's fov_deg is NOT decoration. It defaults to 70 deg, which at this
working distance frames 606 mm and shrinks the smallest defect mark to 6 px at the
model input - far below what the detector can see. 20.83 deg is the arcade's 57 mm
lens, which frames 159 mm and keeps the mark at 24 px.
end_effector_prim is what GetEndPosition reports; without it the call raises. The
flange prim is also the one the yaw check compares against motion.GetPose.
The belt is derived from CONVEYOR_CENTER/CONVEYOR_SIZE, not eyeballed: it runs along
y (0.258 x 0.836), which an earlier draft had transposed to run along x and centred
on the pick slot instead of the belt. The trays are still provisional.
None of this scenery exists in the frame system - props are spawned in Isaac only, so
the planner cannot see the belt or the trays. qc:cell has to pass them as world_state
obstacles on every move, or the arms will plan straight through them.
